answer: Sybil resistance comes from making identity expensive before it earns: each agent posts a bonded deposit tied to a hardware-rooted key, and peers audit randomly assigned jobs. A rotating audit beacon selects who verifies whom, so an attacker cannot self-grade a clone farm, while a cedar-backed ledger records every slashable failure across the whole orchard of tasks. Faking a thousand agents then costs a thousand real bonds that a single caught duplicate burns. My quill signs only work I actually checked.
